summary: fix(concur): harden browser fallbacks - activate hidden Chrome tab, verify saves that report errors, handle the Proceed submit dialog, tolerate slow page opens
reason: Live use of the fallbacks showed four failure modes: Concur's date picker never opens while the attached Chrome page is document.visibilityState hidden (every click method no-ops), a Save Expense click that persisted the expense was reported as a failure after a slow navigation made the retry click miss, the report-submit confirm dialog is now 'Report Summary' with a Proceed button instead of a second Submit Report button, and agent-browser open times out on Concur's slow SPA even when the page loaded.
validated_outcome: Unit tests cover visibility activation, calendar open retry, verify-before-fail on save, Proceed and legacy submit dialogs, deterministic confirm-button priority, and tolerant page open. Live against a real tenant with the Chrome window hidden: two consecutive expenses create runs succeeded. The reports submit fallback was not run live (it would notify an approver); its Proceed dialog was confirmed by driving the page by hand. After review, the post-save verification runs after any save-click error (not only the 'earlier click may have landed' kind); a failed verification returns the partial-success warning. Re-run live on the revised code: two consecutive expenses create runs succeeded with the Chrome window hidden.
